title: The Book of Exodus Decoded
author: Brittany Johnson
description: The Book of Exodus — every verse decoded into plain, modern English (DMLV).

verses.kjv: Now these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.
verses.decoded: These are the names of the descendants of Israel who came to Egypt; each man came with his family, along with Jacob.

verses.kjv: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,
verses.decoded: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin.

verses.kjv: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
verses.decoded: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin were among them.

verses.kjv: Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
verses.decoded: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

verses.kjv: And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt already.
verses.decoded: All the direct descendants of Jacob numbered seventy people, because Joseph was already in Egypt.

verses.kjv: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.
verses.decoded: Joseph died, as did all his brothers and that entire generation.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.
verses.decoded: The descendants of Israel had many children, and their numbers grew greatly; they became very numerous and extremely powerful, and the land was populated by them.

verses.kjv: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.
verses.decoded: Then a new king came to power in Egypt who had no knowledge of Joseph.

verses.kjv: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we:
verses.decoded: He then said to his people, 'Look, the people of Israel are now more numerous and powerful than we are.'

verses.kjv: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.
verses.decoded: Let us act shrewdly against them; otherwise, they will continue to increase in number, and if a war breaks out, they might join our enemies, fight against us, and then escape from the land.

verses.kjv: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.
verses.decoded: Therefore, they appointed taskmasters over them to oppress them with heavy labor. And they built for Pharaoh storage cities, Pithom and Raamses.

verses.kjv: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.
verses.decoded: However, the more the Egyptians oppressed the Israelites, the more the Israelites increased in number and grew. And the Egyptians were distressed because of the Israelites.

verses.kjv: And the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour:
verses.decoded: And the Egyptians forced the descendants of Israel to serve with harshness.

verses.kjv: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.
verses.decoded: And they made their lives miserable with harsh forced labor, in mixing mortar and making bricks, and in all kinds of work in the fields. All the work they forced them to do was carried out with severity.

verses.kjv: And the king of Egypt spake to the Hebrew midwives, of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah:
verses.decoded: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom was named Shiphrah, and the other was named Puah.

verses.kjv: And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.
verses.decoded: And he said, "When you assist the Hebrew women as midwives, and you see them on the birthing stools; if the child is a son, then you must kill him: but if the child is a daughter, then she must live."

verses.kjv: But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.
verses.decoded: However, the midwives respected God and did not do as the king of Egypt commanded them; instead, they allowed the male infants to live.

verses.kjv: And the king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said unto them, Why have ye done this thing, and have saved the men children alive?
verses.decoded: Then the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and said to them, 'Why have you done this thing and allowed the male children to live?'

verses.kjv: And the midwives said unto Pharaoh, Because the Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women; for they are lively, and are delivered ere the midwives come in unto them.
verses.decoded: And the midwives told Pharaoh, "Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous, and they give birth before the midwives arrive to them."

verses.kjv: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.
verses.decoded: Therefore, God showed favor to the midwives, and the people increased in number and became very strong.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses.
verses.decoded: And it happened that because the midwives revered God, he established their households.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.
verses.decoded: Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, 'Every male child who is born, you must throw into the river, but every female child you must allow to live.'

verses.kjv: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.
verses.decoded: A man from the tribe of Levi married a woman who was also from the tribe of Levi.

verses.kjv: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.
verses.decoded: The woman became pregnant and gave birth to a son; and when she saw that he was a beautiful child, she hid him for three months.

verses.kjv: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.
verses.decoded: When she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket for him out of papyrus reeds, sealed it with natural tar and pitch, and placed the child inside; then she set it among the reeds at the edge of the river.

verses.kjv: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.
verses.decoded: And his sister stood at a distance to find out what would happen to him.

verses.kjv: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.
verses.decoded: And Pharaoh's daughter went down to bathe in the river; and her female attendants walked beside the river. When she saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her...

verses.kjv: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.
verses.decoded: And when she opened it, she saw the child; and look, the baby was crying. And she felt pity for him, and said, This is one of the Hebrew children.

verses.kjv: Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?
verses.decoded: Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, 'Should I go and find a nurse from the Hebrew women for you, so that she can nurse the child for you?'

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, Go. And the maid went and called the child’s mother.
verses.decoded: Pharaoh's daughter told her, 'Go.' So the young woman went and summoned the child's mother.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.
verses.decoded: Pharaoh's daughter said to her, 'Take this baby and nurse him for me, and I will pay you for your work.' So the woman took the baby and nursed him.

verses.kjv: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
verses.decoded: When the child grew older, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, 'Because I drew him out of the water.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.
verses.decoded: It happened in those days, after Moses had grown up, that he went out to his fellow Israelites and observed their hard labor. He then saw an Egyptian man beating a Hebrew man, who was one of his own people.

verses.kjv: And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.
verses.decoded: He looked around in every direction, and when he saw that no one was present, he killed the Egyptian and concealed the body in the sand.

verses.kjv: And when he went out the second day, behold, two men of the Hebrews strove together: and he said to him that did the wrong, Wherefore smitest thou thy fellow?
verses.decoded: And when he went out on the second day, he saw two Hebrew men fighting with each other. And he said to the one who was in the wrong, "Why are you hitting your countryman?"

verses.kjv: And he said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? And Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.
verses.decoded: And he said, 'Who appointed you as a ruler and judge over us? Do you intend to kill me, just as you killed the Egyptian?' And Moses was afraid, and said, 'Surely this matter has become known.'

verses.kjv: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
verses.decoded: When Pharaoh heard about this event, he tried to kill Moses. However, Moses escaped from Pharaoh and lived in the land of Midian, where he settled down by a well.

verses.kjv: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.
verses.decoded: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came and drew water, and then filled the watering troughs to provide water for their father's sheep.

verses.kjv: And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
verses.decoded: Then some shepherds arrived and chased them away, but Moses stood up, came to their aid, and watered their sheep.

verses.kjv: And when they came to Reuel their father, he said, How is it that ye are come so soon to day?
verses.decoded: When they came to their father Reuel, he asked, 'Why have you returned so early today?'

verses.kjv: And they said, An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock.
verses.decoded: And they replied, 'An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and also drew enough water for us, and watered the flock.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that ye have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.
verses.decoded: And he said to his daughters, "Then where is he? Why have you left the man? Call him, so that he may eat food."

verses.kjv: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.
verses.decoded: And Moses was agreeable to live with the man, and the man gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses.

verses.kjv: And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.
verses.decoded: And she gave birth to a son, and he named him Gershom, because he said, 'I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto God by reason of the bondage.
verses.decoded: After a long period, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned because of their enslavement, and they cried out, and their cries for help, due to their enslavement, reached God.

verses.kjv: And God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
verses.decoded: And God heard their cries of distress, and God recalled his solemn agreement with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

verses.kjv: And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.
verses.decoded: And God observed the Israelites, and God acknowledged their situation.

verses.kjv: Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb.
verses.decoded: Moses was tending the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and arrived at Horeb, the mountain of God.

verses.kjv: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
verses.decoded: Then the messenger of the Lord appeared to him in a blaze of fire from the middle of a bush. And he looked, and saw that the bush was burning with fire, yet the bush was not being destroyed.

verses.kjv: And Moses said, I will now turn aside, and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
verses.decoded: And Moses said, 'I will now go closer to investigate this remarkable sight, to understand why the bush is not consumed by the fire.'

verses.kjv: And when the LORD saw that he turned aside to see, God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.
verses.decoded: When the Lord saw that he turned to look, God called to him from within the bush and said, 'Moses, Moses!'

verses.kjv: And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
verses.decoded: And he said, Do not come any closer here; take off your sandals from your feet, because the ground on which you are standing is sacred.

verses.kjv: Moreover he said, I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.
verses.decoded: Furthermore, he said, 'I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.' And Moses hid his face because he was afraid to look at God.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows;
verses.decoded: And the Lord said, I have certainly seen the suffering of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cries because of their oppressors; for I know their pain.

verses.kjv: And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.decoded: Therefore, I have descended to rescue them from the control of the Egyptians and to lead them up from that region into a fertile and expansive land, a land abundant with milk and honey; specifically, to the territory inhabited by the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.

verses.kjv: Now therefore, behold, the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: and I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.
verses.decoded: So now, pay attention: the cries of the people of Israel have reached me, and I have also seen the harsh treatment with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.

verses.kjv: Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.
verses.decoded: Therefore, come now, and I will send you to Pharaoh, so that you can bring my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?
verses.decoded: And Moses said to God, "Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and lead the people of Israel out of Egypt?"

verses.kjv: And he said, Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain.
verses.decoded: And he said, I will certainly be with you; and this will be a sign to you that I have sent you: When you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will serve God on this mountain.

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto God, Behold, when I come unto the children of Israel, and shall say unto them, The God of your fathers hath sent me unto you; and they shall say to me, What is his name? what shall I say unto them?
verses.decoded: And Moses said to God, "Look, when I go to the people of Israel and tell them, 'The God of your ancestors has sent me to you,' and they ask me, 'What is his name?' what should I tell them?"

verses.kjv: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.
verses.decoded: And God said to Moses, "I am who I am." And he said, "This is what you are to say to the Israelites: 'I Am has sent me to you.'

verses.kjv: And God said moreover unto Moses, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.
verses.decoded: And God also said to Moses, 'You are to say this to the people of Israel: The LORD, the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you. This is my name eternally, and this is how I am to be remembered for all future generations.'

verses.kjv: Go, and gather the elders of Israel together, and say unto them, The LORD God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, appeared unto me, saying, I have surely visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Egypt:
verses.decoded: Go and assemble the elders of Israel, and tell them, 'The Lord, the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—has appeared to me.'

verses.kjv: And I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt unto the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, unto a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.decoded: And I have declared that I will lead you out of the suffering in Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—a land abundant with milk and honey.

verses.kjv: And they shall hearken to thy voice: and thou shalt come, thou and the elders of Israel, unto the king of Egypt, and ye shall say unto him, The LORD God of the Hebrews hath met with us: and now let us go, we beseech thee, three days’ journey into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.
verses.decoded: And they will listen to your voice, and you, along with the elders of Israel, will go to the king of Egypt, and you will say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now, we ask you, let us go a three-day journey into the wilderness, so that we may offer sacrifices to the LORD our God.'

verses.kjv: And I am sure that the king of Egypt will not let you go, no, not by a mighty hand.
verses.decoded: And I am certain that the king of Egypt will not allow you to leave, not even under duress from a powerful display of force.

verses.kjv: And I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.
verses.decoded: And I will extend my power, and strike Egypt with all the miraculous deeds that I will perform among them; and after that, he will allow you to depart.

verses.kjv: And I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty:
verses.decoded: And I will grant this people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, and it will happen that when you leave, you will not leave empty-handed.

verses.kjv: But every woman shall borrow of her neighbour, and of her that sojourneth in her house, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment: and ye shall put them upon your sons, and upon your daughters; and ye shall spoil the Egyptians.
verses.decoded: However, each woman will ask her neighbor, and any woman living in her house, for articles made of silver, articles made of gold, and clothing. You will then put these items on your sons and daughters, and in this way, you will take possessions from the Egyptians.

verses.kjv: And Moses answered and said, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice: for they will say, The LORD hath not appeared unto thee.
verses.decoded: Then Moses replied, "But look, they will not believe me or listen to what I say, because they will claim that the LORD has not appeared to you."

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto him, What is that in thine hand? And he said, A rod.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord asked him, 'What is that in your hand?' And he replied, 'A staff.'

verses.kjv: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
verses.decoded: Then he said, 'Throw it on the ground.' And he threw it on the ground, and it turned into a snake; and Moses ran away from it.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Put forth thine hand, and take it by the tail. And he put forth his hand, and caught it, and it became a rod in his hand:
verses.decoded: Then the Lord instructed Moses, 'Reach out your hand and grasp it by its tail.' So Moses extended his hand, seized it, and it transformed into a staff in his hand.

verses.kjv: That they may believe that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.
verses.decoded: So that they may believe that the Lord God of their ancestors, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said furthermore unto him, Put now thine hand into thy bosom. And he put his hand into his bosom: and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous as snow.
verses.decoded: And the LORD also said to him, 'Now put your hand inside your cloak.' So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out, his hand was diseased with leprosy, as white as snow.

verses.kjv: And he said, Put thine hand into thy bosom again. And he put his hand into his bosom again; and plucked it out of his bosom, and, behold, it was turned again as his other flesh.
verses.decoded: Then he said, "Put your hand back into your cloak." So he put his hand back into his cloak, and when he took it out, it was restored to be like the rest of his skin.

verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe thee, neither hearken to the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.
verses.decoded: And it will happen that if they do not believe you, nor heed the evidence of the first miraculous sign, then they will believe the evidence of the subsequent miraculous sign.

verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, if they will not believe also these two signs, neither hearken unto thy voice, that thou shalt take of the water of the river, and pour it upon the dry land: and the water which thou takest out of the river shall become blood upon the dry land.
verses.decoded: And it will happen, if they do not believe these two signs as well, nor listen to your voice, that you must take some water from the river and pour it onto the dry ground; and the water you take from the river will turn into blood on the dry ground.

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto the LORD, O my LORD, I am not eloquent, neither heretofore, nor since thou hast spoken unto thy servant: but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
verses.decoded: And Moses said to the Lord, "Oh my Lord, I am not a skilled speaker, neither in the past nor since you have spoken to your servant; instead, I am slow in speaking and have difficulty articulating words."

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto him, Who hath made man’s mouth? or who maketh the dumb, or deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? have not I the LORD?
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to him, 'Who created a person's mouth? Or who makes someone unable to speak, or unable to hear, or able to see, or unable to see? Is it not I, the Lord?'

verses.kjv: Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.
verses.decoded: So now, go, and I will help you speak, and I will instruct you on what you are to say.

verses.kjv: And he said, O my LORD, send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send.
verses.decoded: And he said, 'Oh, my Lord, please send someone else whom you wish to send.'

verses.kjv: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses, and he said, Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well. And also, behold, he cometh forth to meet thee: and when he seeth thee, he will be glad in his heart.
verses.decoded: And the LORD's anger was ignited against Moses, and he said, "Is not Aaron, your brother, the Levite? I know that he is a skilled speaker."

verses.kjv: And thou shalt speak unto him, and put words in his mouth: and I will be with thy mouth, and with his mouth, and will teach you what ye shall do.
verses.decoded: And you are to speak to him, and provide him with the words to say; and I will guide both your speech and his speech, and instruct you both on what you are to do.

verses.kjv: And he shall be thy spokesman unto the people: and he shall be, even he shall be to thee instead of a mouth, and thou shalt be to him instead of God.
verses.decoded: And he will speak for you to the people: and he will serve as your voice, and you will be to him as God.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do signs.
verses.decoded: And you are to take this staff in your hand, with which you will perform miraculous signs.

verses.kjv: And Moses went and returned to Jethro his father in law, and said unto him, Let me go, I pray thee, and return unto my brethren which are in Egypt, and see whether they be yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.
verses.decoded: Then Moses went back to Jethro, his father-in-law, and said to him, 'Please let me go and return to my relatives who are in Egypt, to see if they are still alive.' And Jethro said to Moses, 'Go in peace.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses while he was in Midian, 'Go, return to Egypt, because all the men who were trying to kill you have died.'

verses.kjv: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt: and Moses took the rod of God in his hand.
verses.decoded: Moses took his wife and his sons, placed them on a donkey, and returned to the land of Egypt. Moses also took the staff of God in his hand.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, When thou goest to return into Egypt, see that thou do all those wonders before Pharaoh, which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord instructed Moses, 'When you return to Egypt, ensure that you perform all the miraculous deeds before Pharaoh that I have enabled you to do. However, I will make his heart resistant, so that he will not release the people.'

verses.kjv: And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD, Israel is my son, even my firstborn:
verses.decoded: Then you are to tell Pharaoh: 'This is what the LORD says: Israel is my son, my firstborn.'

verses.kjv: And I say unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me: and if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.
verses.decoded: And I tell you, release my son so that he may serve me. If you refuse to release him, then I will kill your son, your firstborn.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him.
verses.decoded: And it happened on the journey at the lodging place, that the Lord encountered him and intended to kill him.

verses.kjv: Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.
verses.decoded: Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and threw it at his feet, and said, "Indeed, you are to me a husband of blood."

verses.kjv: So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.
verses.decoded: So he released him. Then she said, 'You are a husband by blood, because of the circumcision.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses. And he went, and met him in the mount of God, and kissed him.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord instructed Aaron, 'Go into the wilderness to meet Moses.' So Aaron went, and he met Moses at the mountain of God, and greeted him with a kiss.

verses.kjv: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD who had sent him, and all the signs which he had commanded him.
verses.decoded: Moses informed Aaron of everything the Lord, who had sent him, had said, and all the miraculous signs the Lord had instructed him to perform.

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel:
verses.decoded: Then Moses and Aaron went and assembled all the elders of the Israelites:

verses.kjv: And Aaron spake all the words which the LORD had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.
verses.decoded: And Aaron spoke all the words that the Lord had spoken to Moses, and performed the miraculous signs for the people to see.

verses.kjv: And the people believed: and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.
verses.decoded: And the people believed. And when they heard that the Lord had come to the Israelites and had seen their suffering, they bowed down and worshipped.

verses.kjv: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.
verses.decoded: After this, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and told him, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Let my people go, so that they may celebrate a festival for me in the wilderness.'"

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh said, Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice to let Israel go? I know not the LORD, neither will I let Israel go.
verses.decoded: And Pharaoh said, "Who is the Lord, that I should obey his command to release Israel? I do not know the Lord, nor will I release Israel."

verses.kjv: And they said, The God of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days’ journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto the LORD our God; lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.
verses.decoded: And they said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the LORD our God."

verses.kjv: And the king of Egypt said unto them, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens.
verses.decoded: And the king of Egypt said to them, 'Why do you, Moses and Aaron, distract the people from their work? Go back to your own tasks.'

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh said, Behold, the people of the land now are many, and ye make them rest from their burdens.
verses.decoded: And Pharaoh said, "Look, the people of this land are now numerous, and you are causing them to stop working from their labors."

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh commanded the same day the taskmasters of the people, and their officers, saying,
verses.decoded: And that same day, Pharaoh gave orders to the slave drivers and their foremen, saying,

verses.kjv: Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.
verses.decoded: You will no longer give the people straw to make bricks, as you have done previously; let them go and gather straw for themselves.

verses.kjv: And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.
verses.decoded: And the quota of bricks, which they made previously, you shall impose upon them; you shall not reduce any of it: because they are idle; therefore.

verses.kjv: Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words.
verses.decoded: Let more work be imposed on these men, so that they must labor at it; and let them not pay attention to empty promises.

verses.kjv: And the taskmasters of the people went out, and their officers, and they spake to the people, saying, Thus saith Pharaoh, I will not give you straw.
verses.decoded: The supervisors of the people and their foremen went out and spoke to the people, saying, 'Pharaoh declares this: I will no longer provide you with straw.'

verses.kjv: Go ye, get you straw where ye can find it: yet not ought of your work shall be diminished.
verses.decoded: You all go and get yourselves straw wherever you can find it; however, none of your required work will be reduced.

verses.kjv: So the people were scattered abroad throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble instead of straw.
verses.decoded: Consequently, the people were dispersed throughout the entire land of Egypt to collect stubble in place of straw.

verses.kjv: And the taskmasters hasted them, saying, Fulfil your works, your daily tasks, as when there was straw.
verses.decoded: And the overseers hurried them, saying, 'Complete your assigned labor, your daily quotas, just as you did when straw was provided.'

verses.kjv: And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick both yesterday and to day, as heretofore?
verses.decoded: And the Israelite foremen, whom Pharaoh's slave drivers had appointed over them, were beaten and forcefully asked, 'Why have you not completed your assigned work?'

verses.kjv: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried unto Pharaoh, saying, Wherefore dealest thou thus with thy servants?
verses.decoded: Then the foremen of the Israelites came and complained to Pharaoh, saying, "Why do you treat your servants in this manner?"

verses.kjv: There is no straw given unto thy servants, and they say to us, Make brick: and, behold, thy servants are beaten; but the fault is in thine own people.
verses.decoded: Your servants are not given any straw, yet they demand that we make bricks. And indeed, your servants are being beaten, but the blame lies with your own people.

verses.kjv: But he said, Ye are idle, ye are idle: therefore ye say, Let us go and do sacrifice to the LORD.
verses.decoded: But he said, 'You are lazy, you are lazy; that is why you say, "Let us go and offer sacrifices to the Lord."'

verses.kjv: Go therefore now, and work; for there shall no straw be given you, yet shall ye deliver the tale of bricks.
verses.decoded: So go now and work; because you will not be given any straw, yet you must still produce the required number of bricks.

verses.kjv: And the officers of the children of Israel did see that they were in evil case, after it was said, Ye shall not minish ought from your bricks of your daily task.
verses.decoded: And the foremen of the Israelites realized they were in a difficult situation after it was declared that they must not reduce any of the bricks from their daily quota.

verses.kjv: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood in the way, as they came forth from Pharaoh:
verses.decoded: And they encountered Moses and Aaron, who were standing on the path, as they were coming out from Pharaoh's presence:

verses.kjv: And they said unto them, The LORD look upon you, and judge; because ye have made our savour to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us.
verses.decoded: And they said to them, "May the Lord observe you and judge you, because you have made our reputation detestable in the sight of Pharaoh and his officials, giving them a reason to kill us."

verses.kjv: And Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, LORD, wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me?
verses.decoded: And Moses returned to the Lord and said, 'Lord, why have you treated this people so badly? Why is it that you sent me?'

verses.kjv: For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all.
verses.decoded: Because ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has treated this people badly; and you have not rescued your people at all.

verses.kjv: Then the LORD said unto Moses, Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh: for with a strong hand shall he let them go, and with a strong hand shall he drive them out of his land.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh. Because with a powerful display of force, he will let them go, and with a powerful display of force, he will drive them out of his land.'

verses.kjv: And God spake unto Moses, and said unto him, I am the LORD:
verses.decoded: And God spoke to Moses and said to him, I am the LORD.

verses.kjv: And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty, but by my name JEHOVAH was I not known to them.
verses.decoded: And I revealed myself to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob by the name God Almighty, but I did not make my name JEHOVAH known to them.

verses.kjv: And I have also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their pilgrimage, wherein they were strangers.
verses.decoded: And I have also confirmed my solemn agreement with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land where they resided as temporary inhabitants, in which they were foreigners.

verses.kjv: And I have also heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians keep in bondage; and I have remembered my covenant.
verses.decoded: Furthermore, I have heard the cries of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians have enslaved, and I have remembered my covenant.

verses.kjv: Wherefore say unto the children of Israel, I am the LORD, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will rid you out of their bondage, and I will redeem you with a stretched out arm, and with great judgments:
verses.decoded: Therefore, tell the Israelites, 'I am the Lord, and I will free you from the heavy labor imposed by the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from their slavery, and I will rescue you with my powerful hand, and with significant acts of justice.'

verses.kjv: And I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God: and ye shall know that I am the LORD your God, which bringeth you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
verses.decoded: And I will claim you as my own people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am the Lord your God, who is leading you out from under the heavy labor imposed by the Egyptians.

verses.kjv: And I will bring you in unto the land, concerning the which I did swear to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it you for an heritage: I am the LORD.
verses.decoded: And I will bring you into the land, which I solemnly promised to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it to you as an inheritance: I am the Lord.

verses.kjv: And Moses spake so unto the children of Israel: but they hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit, and for cruel bondage.
verses.decoded: And Moses spoke these words to the Israelites, but they did not listen to him because of their deep distress and harsh slavery.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.decoded: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

verses.kjv: Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.decoded: Go and speak to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, so that he will allow the people of Israel to leave his country.

verses.kjv: And Moses spake before the LORD, saying, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips?
verses.decoded: And Moses spoke to the Lord, saying, 'Look, the people of Israel have not listened to me; so how will Pharaoh listen to me, since I am not eloquent?'

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, and gave them a charge unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and gave them a command concerning the Israelites and concerning Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to lead the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: These be the heads of their fathers’ houses: The sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel; Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi: these be the families of Reuben.
verses.decoded: These are the leaders of their ancestral families: The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the family groups of Reuben.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman: these are the families of Simeon.
verses.decoded: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, whose mother was a Canaanite woman. These are the ancestral groups of Simeon.

verses.kjv: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations; Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari: and the years of the life of Levi were an hundred thirty and seven years.
verses.decoded: These are the names of Levi's sons, listed by their family lines: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived for one hundred thirty-seven years.

verses.kjv: The sons of Gershon; Libni, and Shimi, according to their families.
verses.decoded: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimi, each forming their own family groups.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Kohath; Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel: and the years of the life of Kohath were an hundred thirty and three years.
verses.decoded: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived for one hundred thirty-three years.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Merari; Mahali and Mushi: these are the families of Levi according to their generations.
verses.decoded: The sons of Merari were Mahali and Mushi. These are the clans descended from Levi, listed by their lineage.

verses.kjv: And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to wife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were an hundred and thirty and seven years.
verses.decoded: Amram married Jochebed, who was his father's sister. She gave birth to Aaron and Moses. Amram lived for one hundred and thirty-seven years.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Izhar; Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
verses.decoded: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Uzziel; Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Zithri.
verses.decoded: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Zithri.

verses.kjv: And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.decoded: Aaron married Elisheba, who was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Naashon; and she gave birth to his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Korah; Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph: these are the families of the Korhites.
verses.decoded: The sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the family lines of the Korahites.

verses.kjv: And Eleazar Aaron’s son took him one of the daughters of Putiel to wife; and she bare him Phinehas: these are the heads of the fathers of the Levites according to their families.
verses.decoded: And Eleazar, Aaron's son, took one of Putiel's daughters as his wife; and she gave birth to Phinehas. These are the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Levites, according to their families.

verses.kjv: These are that Aaron and Moses, to whom the LORD said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their armies.
verses.decoded: These were Aaron and Moses, to whom the Lord commanded, 'Bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt, organized into their divisions.'

verses.kjv: These are they which spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt: these are that Moses and Aaron.
verses.decoded: These are the ones who spoke to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, to lead the Israelites out of Egypt; these are Moses and Aaron.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass on the day when the LORD spake unto Moses in the land of Egypt,
verses.decoded: It happened on the day that the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: That the LORD spake unto Moses, saying, I am the LORD: speak thou unto Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I say unto thee.
verses.decoded: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, I am the LORD: speak to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, everything that I tell you.

verses.kjv: And Moses said before the LORD, Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips, and how shall Pharaoh hearken unto me?
verses.decoded: Then Moses said to the Lord, "Look, I am a poor speaker, so how will Pharaoh listen to me?"

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, See, I have made thee a god to Pharaoh: and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, "Understand this: I have appointed you as a divine authority to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will serve as your spokesman."

verses.kjv: Thou shalt speak all that I command thee: and Aaron thy brother shall speak unto Pharaoh, that he send the children of Israel out of his land.
verses.decoded: You must say everything I instruct you to say, and your brother Aaron will speak to Pharaoh so that he will let the Israelites leave his country.

verses.kjv: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and multiply my signs and my wonders in the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: I will make Pharaoh stubborn, and I will increase my miraculous signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.
verses.decoded: But Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that I may bring my power upon Egypt and lead out my people, the Israelites, from the land of Egypt through great acts of judgment.

verses.kjv: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I stretch forth mine hand upon Egypt, and bring out the children of Israel from among them.
verses.decoded: And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I extend my power over Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron did as the LORD commanded them, so did they.
verses.decoded: So Moses and Aaron did exactly as the LORD commanded them.

verses.kjv: And Moses was fourscore years old, and Aaron fourscore and three years old, when they spake unto Pharaoh.
verses.decoded: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron was eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
verses.decoded: And the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

verses.kjv: When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Shew a miracle for you: then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it before Pharaoh, and it shall become a serpent.
verses.decoded: When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, 'Perform a miracle for yourselves,' then you shall say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh,' and it will become a snake.

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as the LORD had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
verses.decoded: Then Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh, and they did exactly as the Lord had instructed. Aaron threw his staff down in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and it turned into a snake.

verses.kjv: Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments.
verses.decoded: Then Pharaoh also summoned the wise men and the sorcerers; and the Egyptian magicians likewise performed similar feats with their secret arts.

verses.kjv: For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.
verses.decoded: Because each of them threw down his staff, and their staffs turned into snakes, but Aaron's staff swallowed their staffs.

verses.kjv: And he hardened Pharaoh’s heart, that he hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had said.
verses.decoded: And he made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, so that he would not listen to them, just as the Lord had predicted.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Pharaoh’s heart is hardened, he refuseth to let the people go.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, Pharaoh's heart is stubborn, he refuses to let the people go.

verses.kjv: Get thee unto Pharaoh in the morning; lo, he goeth out unto the water; and thou shalt stand by the river’s brink against he come; and the rod which was turned to a serpent shalt thou take in thine hand.
verses.decoded: Go to Pharaoh in the morning; behold, he is going out to the water; and you shall stand by the river's edge when he comes; and you shall take the staff that was turned into a snake in your hand.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt say unto him, The LORD God of the Hebrews hath sent me unto thee, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness: and, behold, hitherto thou wouldest not hear.
verses.decoded: And you are to say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, "Let my people go, so that they may serve me in the wilderness." But indeed, up until now you have not listened!'

verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, In this thou shalt know that I am the LORD: behold, I will smite with the rod that is in mine hand upon the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.
verses.decoded: This is what the LORD says: By this action, you will know that I am the LORD. Pay attention: I will strike the waters in the river with the staff that is in my hand,

verses.kjv: And the fish that is in the river shall die, and the river shall stink; and the Egyptians shall lothe to drink of the water of the river.
verses.decoded: The fish in the river will die, and the river will become foul-smelling; consequently, the Egyptians will find it repulsive to drink the river's water.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the waters of Egypt, upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and that there may be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and in vessels of stone.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your staff and extend your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their canals, their rivers, their ponds, and all their reservoirs—so that they may turn into blood. There will be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, even in wooden and stone containers.'

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron did so, as the LORD commanded; and he lifted up the rod, and smote the waters that were in the river, in the sight of Pharaoh, and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
verses.decoded: And Moses and Aaron acted accordingly, just as the Lord had instructed; and he raised the staff and struck the water in the river, in the presence of Pharaoh and his officials; and all the water in the river was transformed into blood.

verses.kjv: And the fish that was in the river died; and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink of the water of the river; and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: The fish in the river died; the river became foul-smelling, and the Egyptians were unable to drink the river's water; and there was blood throughout the entire land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And the magicians of Egypt did so with their enchantments: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, neither did he hearken unto them; as the LORD had said.
verses.decoded: And the Egyptian sorcerers performed the same actions with their magical arts; and Pharaoh's resolve became unyielding, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had foretold.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, neither did he set his heart to this also.
verses.decoded: And Pharaoh turned and went into his palace, and he did not give serious consideration to this matter either.

verses.kjv: And all the Egyptians digged round about the river for water to drink; for they could not drink of the water of the river.
verses.decoded: And all the Egyptians dug around the river in search of water to drink, because they were unable to drink the water from the river itself.

verses.kjv: And seven days were fulfilled, after that the LORD had smitten the river.
verses.decoded: A full seven days had passed after the LORD had struck the Nile River.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, Go unto Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.decoded: And the Lord spoke to Moses, 'Go to Pharaoh and say to him, "This is what the Lord says: Let my people go, so that they may serve me."'

verses.kjv: And if thou refuse to let them go, behold, I will smite all thy borders with frogs:
verses.decoded: And if you refuse to let them go, then I will strike all your territory with frogs.

verses.kjv: And the river shall bring forth frogs abundantly, which shall go up and come into thine house, and into thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneadingtroughs:
verses.decoded: The river will produce an abundance of frogs, and they will go up and enter your house, your bedroom, and onto your bed, and into the houses of your officials, and onto your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneading bowls.

verses.kjv: And the frogs shall come up both on thee, and upon thy people, and upon all thy servants.
verses.decoded: And the frogs will come up on you, and on your people, and on all your servants.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch forth thine hand with thy rod over the streams, over the rivers, and over the ponds, and cause frogs to come up upon the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, 'Tell Aaron to extend his hand with his staff over the canals, over the rivers, and over the marshes, and cause frogs to come up onto the land of Egypt.'

verses.kjv: And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt; and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: Then Aaron extended his hand over the waters of Egypt, and frogs emerged and spread across the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And the magicians did so with their enchantments, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And the sorcerers performed the same action using their magical spells, causing frogs to appear throughout the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, Intreat the LORD, that he may take away the frogs from me, and from my people; and I will let the people go, that they may do sacrifice unto the LORD.
verses.decoded: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Plead with the LORD to remove the frogs from me and my people, and I will let the people go so that they may offer sacrifices to the LORD."

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto Pharaoh, Glory over me: when shall I intreat for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, to destroy the frogs from thee and thy houses, that they may remain in the river only?
verses.decoded: Then Moses said to Pharaoh, 'You may tell me when I should pray for you, your officials, and your people, that the frogs may be removed from you and your homes, and remain only in the Nile River.'

verses.kjv: And he said, To morrow. And he said, Be it according to thy word: that thou mayest know that there is none like unto the LORD our God.
verses.decoded: And he said, "Tomorrow." And he said, "It will be as you have spoken, so that you may know that there is no one like the Lord our God."

verses.kjv: And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy houses, and from thy servants, and from thy people; they shall remain in the river only.
verses.decoded: And the frogs will leave you, your homes, your servants, and your people; they will remain only in the river.

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh: and Moses cried unto the LORD because of the frogs which he had brought against Pharaoh.
verses.decoded: Then Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh. And Moses appealed to the Lord concerning the frogs that He had sent against Pharaoh.

verses.kjv: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses; and the frogs died out of the houses, out of the villages, and out of the fields.
verses.decoded: And the Lord acted in accordance with Moses' command; and the frogs died in the houses, in the villages, and in the fields.

verses.kjv: And they gathered them together upon heaps: and the land stank.
verses.decoded: And the Egyptians gathered the dead frogs into piles, and the land smelled foul.

verses.kjv: But when Pharaoh saw that there was respite, he hardened his heart, and hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had said.
verses.decoded: But when Pharaoh observed that there was a temporary relief, he became stubborn and refused to listen to them, just as the Lord had foretold.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Tell Aaron to extend his staff and strike the dust of the ground, so that it may become gnats throughout all the land of Egypt."

verses.kjv: And they did so; for Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod, and smote the dust of the earth, and it became lice in man, and in beast; all the dust of the land became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And they did as commanded; for Aaron extended his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the ground, and it turned into gnats on both people and animals; all the dust of the land became gnats throughout the entire land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And the magicians did so with their enchantments to bring forth lice, but they could not: so there were lice upon man, and upon beast.
verses.decoded: The magicians attempted to use their secret arts to produce gnats, but they were unable to do so. Consequently, gnats remained on both people and animals.

verses.kjv: Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had said.
verses.decoded: Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, 'This is a divine act.' But Pharaoh's resolve remained firm, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had stated.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh; lo, he cometh forth to the water; and say unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh; look, he is coming out to the water. And say to him, 'This is what the Lord says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me.'"

verses.kjv: Else, if thou wilt not let my people go, behold, I will send swarms of flies upon thee, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thy houses: and the houses of the Egyptians shall be full of swarms of flies, and also the ground whereon they are.
verses.decoded: Otherwise, if you refuse to release my people, then I will send swarms of insects upon you, your officials, and your people, and into your homes. The houses of the Egyptians will be filled with these swarms, as will the ground they stand on.

verses.kjv: And I will sever in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there; to the end thou mayest know that I am the LORD in the midst of the earth.
verses.decoded: On that day, I will set apart the region of Goshen, where my people reside, so that no swarms of flies will be present there. This is so you may understand that I am the Lord who is present throughout the entire world.

verses.kjv: And I will put a division between my people and thy people: to morrow shall this sign be.
verses.decoded: And I will create a clear distinction between my people and your people; this miraculous sign will occur tomorrow.

verses.kjv: And the LORD did so; and there came a grievous swarm of flies into the house of Pharaoh, and into his servants’ houses, and into all the land of Egypt: the land was corrupted by reason of the swarm of flies.
verses.decoded: And the Lord did as promised; and a severe swarm of flies entered the house of Pharaoh, and the houses of his officials, and all the land of Egypt. The land was ruined because of the swarm of flies.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said, Go ye, sacrifice to your God in the land.
verses.decoded: Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, 'Go, offer sacrifices to your God within this land.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said, It is not meet so to do; for we shall sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to the LORD our God: lo, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us?
verses.decoded: And Moses said, 'It is not appropriate to do that; because we would be sacrificing what the Egyptians consider detestable to the Lord our God. Indeed, if we sacrifice what the Egyptians detest right before their eyes, won't they stone us?'

verses.kjv: We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to the LORD our God, as he shall command us.
verses.decoded: We will travel for three days into the wilderness and offer sacrifices to the Lord our God, just as he instructs us.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh said, I will let you go, that ye may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness; only ye shall not go very far away: intreat for me.
verses.decoded: And Pharaoh said, 'I will allow you to leave, so that you may offer sacrifices to the Lord your God in the desert; however, you must not go too far away. Plead on my behalf.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said, Behold, I go out from thee, and I will intreat the LORD that the swarms of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people, to morrow: but let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more in not letting the people go to sacrifice to the LORD.
verses.decoded: And Moses said, 'Look, I am leaving you, and I will plead with the Lord so that the swarms of flies may leave Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. However, do not let Pharaoh deceive us again by refusing to let the people go to offer sacrifices to the Lord.'

verses.kjv: And Moses went out from Pharaoh, and intreated the LORD.
verses.decoded: And Moses left Pharaoh and pleaded with the Lord.

verses.kjv: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses; and he removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; there remained not one.
verses.decoded: And the Lord acted in accordance with Moses' request; and he removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his officials, and from his people; not a single one remained.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, neither would he let the people go.
verses.decoded: Pharaoh also made his heart stubborn at this time, and he would not let the people leave.

verses.kjv: Then the LORD said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh, and tell him, Thus saith the LORD God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Go to Pharaoh and tell him, "This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me."'

verses.kjv: For if thou refuse to let them go, and wilt hold them still,
verses.decoded: Because if you refuse to release them and continue to hold them captive,

verses.kjv: Behold, the hand of the LORD is upon thy cattle which is in the field, upon the horses, upon the asses, upon the camels, upon the oxen, and upon the sheep: there shall be a very grievous murrain.
verses.decoded: Indeed, the Lord's power will affect your livestock in the fields, specifically your horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, and sheep; a very severe plague will occur.

verses.kjv: And the LORD shall sever between the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt: and there shall nothing die of all that is the children’s of Israel.
verses.decoded: And the Lord will make a distinction between the livestock of the Israelites and the livestock of the Egyptians, so that none of the livestock belonging to the Israelites will die.

verses.kjv: And the LORD appointed a set time, saying, To morrow the LORD shall do this thing in the land.
verses.decoded: And the Lord set a specific time, stating, 'Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing in the land.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD did that thing on the morrow, and all the cattle of Egypt died: but of the cattle of the children of Israel died not one.
verses.decoded: And the LORD carried out that action the next day, and all the livestock belonging to Egypt died; however, not a single animal belonging to the Israelites died.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh sent, and, behold, there was not one of the cattle of the Israelites dead. And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, and he did not let the people go.
verses.decoded: Pharaoh then sent messengers to investigate, and indeed, not a single animal belonging to the Israelites had died. Nevertheless, Pharaoh remained unyielding, and he refused to release the people.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses and unto Aaron, Take to you handfuls of ashes of the furnace, and let Moses sprinkle it toward the heaven in the sight of Pharaoh.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron, 'Take handfuls of ashes from the furnace, and have Moses sprinkle it towards the sky in front of Pharaoh.'

verses.kjv: And it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And it will turn into fine dust all over the land of Egypt, and will cause boils that erupt into festering sores on both people and animals, throughout the entire land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And they took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward heaven; and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast.
verses.decoded: So they took ashes from a kiln, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses threw it into the air toward the sky; and it caused boils to erupt with festering sores on both people and animals.

verses.kjv: And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boil was upon the magicians, and upon all the Egyptians.
verses.decoded: The magicians were unable to remain in Moses' presence due to the boils; indeed, the boils afflicted the magicians as well as all the Egyptians.

verses.kjv: And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had spoken unto Moses.
verses.decoded: And the Lord made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had told Moses would happen.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Rise up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and say unto him, Thus saith the LORD God of the Hebrews, Let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, 'Get up early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and say to him, "This is what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says:"'

verses.kjv: For I will at this time send all my plagues upon thine heart, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people; that thou mayest know that there is none like me in all the earth.
verses.decoded: Because at this time I will send all my devastating afflictions directly against you, and against your officials, and against your people, so that you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth.

verses.kjv: For now I will stretch out my hand, that I may smite thee and thy people with pestilence; and thou shalt be cut off from the earth.
verses.decoded: Because by now I could have extended my power to strike you and your people with a deadly disease, and you would have been eliminated from the earth.

verses.kjv: And in very deed for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power; and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.
verses.decoded: And indeed, for this very reason I have kept you alive, to demonstrate my power through you, and so that my name may be proclaimed throughout the entire earth.

verses.kjv: As yet exaltest thou thyself against my people, that thou wilt not let them go?
verses.decoded: Are you still elevating yourself above my people, refusing to release them?

verses.kjv: Behold, to morrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail, such as hath not been in Egypt since the foundation thereof even until now.
verses.decoded: Look, around this time tomorrow, I will cause a very severe hailstorm to occur, such as has not happened in Egypt since its founding, even up to the present time.

verses.kjv: Send therefore now, and gather thy cattle, and all that thou hast in the field; for upon every man and beast which shall be found in the field, and shall not be brought home, the hail shall come down upon them, and they shall die.
verses.decoded: Therefore, send word now and gather your livestock and everything else you have in the open fields; because for every person and animal that remains in the field and is not brought indoors, hail will fall on them, and they will die.

verses.kjv: He that feared the word of the LORD among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into the houses:
verses.decoded: The one among Pharaoh's officials who respected the Lord's warning caused his servants and his livestock to take refuge in their homes.

verses.kjv: And he that regarded not the word of the LORD left his servants and his cattle in the field.
verses.decoded: But the person who ignored the warning from the Lord left their servants and their livestock out in the field.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch forth thine hand toward heaven, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt, upon man, and upon beast, and upon every herb of the field, throughout the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, 'Extend your hand toward the sky, so that hail may fall throughout the entire land of Egypt, affecting both people, animals, and every plant in the fields.'

verses.kjv: And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven: and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground; and the LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: Then Moses extended his staff toward the sky, and the Lord sent thunder and hail. Fire moved across the ground, and the Lord caused hail to fall.

verses.kjv: So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
verses.decoded: So there was hail, and fire mixed with the hail, which was extremely severe, unlike anything that had occurred in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.

verses.kjv: And the hail smote throughout all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and beast; and the hail smote every herb of the field, and brake every tree of the field.
verses.decoded: And the hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt, affecting everything that was in the open fields, including both people and animals; and the hail struck down every plant in the fields and broke every tree in the fields.

verses.kjv: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, was there no hail.
verses.decoded: Only in the region of Goshen, where the descendants of Israel resided, was there no hail.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh sent, and called for Moses and Aaron, and said unto them, I have sinned this time: the LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
verses.decoded: Then Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron, and he said to them, "I have sinned this time; the Lord is just, and I and my people are in the wrong."

verses.kjv: Intreat the LORD (for it is enough) that there be no more mighty thunderings and hail; and I will let you go, and ye shall stay no longer.
verses.decoded: Plead with the Lord, for this has been enough, that there will be no more powerful thunder and hail; and I will release you, and you will not remain any longer.

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto him, As soon as I am gone out of the city, I will spread abroad my hands unto the LORD; and the thunder shall cease, neither shall there be any more hail; that thou mayest know how that the earth is the LORD’s.
verses.decoded: And Moses said to him, "As soon as I have left the city, I will lift my hands in prayer to the Lord; and the thunder will stop, and there will be no more hail; so that you may know that the earth belongs to the Lord."

verses.kjv: But as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear the LORD God.
verses.decoded: But as for you and your officials, I know that you do not yet revere the Lord God.

verses.kjv: And the flax and the barley was smitten: for the barley was in the ear, and the flax was bolled.
verses.decoded: The flax and the barley were struck down, because the barley had formed heads and the flax had produced seed pods.

verses.kjv: But the wheat and the rie were not smitten: for they were not grown up.
verses.decoded: However, the wheat and the rye were not damaged, because they had not yet grown tall.

verses.kjv: And Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh, and spread abroad his hands unto the LORD: and the thunders and hail ceased, and the rain was not poured upon the earth.
verses.decoded: And Moses went out of the city, away from Pharaoh, and lifted his hands to the Lord. Then the thunder and hail stopped, and the rain no longer fell.

verses.kjv: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunders were ceased, he sinned yet more, and hardened his heart, he and his servants.
verses.decoded: And when Pharaoh observed that the rain, hail, and thunder had stopped, he continued to sin even more, and he, along with his officials, remained stubborn.

verses.kjv: And the heart of Pharaoh was hardened, neither would he let the children of Israel go; as the LORD had spoken by Moses.
verses.decoded: And Pharaoh remained stubborn, refusing to allow the Israelites to leave, just as the Lord had declared through Moses.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go in unto Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants, that I might shew these my signs before him:
verses.decoded: Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh, because I have made his heart stubborn and the hearts of his officials stubborn, so that I could display these miraculous signs of mine before him."

verses.kjv: And that thou mayest tell in the ears of thy son, and of thy son’s son, what things I have wrought in Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that ye may know how that I am the LORD.
verses.decoded: So that you may tell your son and your grandson what I have accomplished in Egypt, and the miraculous signs I performed among them, so that you may know that I am the LORD.

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron came in unto Pharaoh, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD God of the Hebrews, How long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself before me? let my people go, that they may serve me.
verses.decoded: Then Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: 'How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me?'

verses.kjv: Else, if thou refuse to let my people go, behold, to morrow will I bring the locusts into thy coast:
verses.decoded: Otherwise, if you refuse to let my people go, know that tomorrow I will bring locusts into your territory.

verses.kjv: And they shall cover the face of the earth, that one cannot be able to see the earth: and they shall eat the residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth unto you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which groweth for you out of the field:
verses.decoded: And they will cover the surface of the land, so that it will be impossible to see the ground. They will consume what is left over from what survived the hail, and they will eat every tree that grows for you in the field.

verses.kjv: And they shall fill thy houses, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians; which neither thy fathers, nor thy fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they were upon the earth unto this day. And he turned himself, and went out from Pharaoh.
verses.decoded: And they will fill your houses, along with the houses of all your servants and all the Egyptians. This is something neither your ancestors nor your grandfathers have seen from the time they came into existence on the earth until this very day.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh’s servants said unto him, How long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve the LORD their God: knowest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?
