verses.decoded: And Pharaoh's officials said to him, 'How long will this man be a trap for us? Let the men go, so that they may worship the Lord their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt is ruined?'

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron were brought again unto Pharaoh: and he said unto them, Go, serve the LORD your God: but who are they that shall go?
verses.decoded: Then Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. And he said to them, "Go, worship the LORD your God; but who exactly will be going?"

verses.kjv: And Moses said, We will go with our young and with our old, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds will we go; for we must hold a feast unto the LORD.
verses.decoded: And Moses said, We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and our daughters, and with our flocks and our herds; for we must hold a festival to the Lord.

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Let the LORD be so with you, as I will let you go, and your little ones: look to it; for evil is before you.
verses.decoded: And he said to them, 'May the Lord be with you only if I let you go with your young children. Be careful, for trouble is ahead of you.'

verses.kjv: Not so: go now ye that are men, and serve the LORD; for that ye did desire. And they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.
verses.decoded: No, that is not how it will be. Only you men may go now and worship the Lord, because that is what you requested. And they were driven out from Pharaoh's presence.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up upon the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail hath left.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, Extend your hand over the land of Egypt to bring forth the locusts, so that they may spread across the land of Egypt, and consume all the vegetation of the land, including everything that the hail has spared.

verses.kjv: And Moses stretched forth his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD brought an east wind upon the land all that day, and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.
verses.decoded: Then Moses extended his staff over the land of Egypt, and the Lord caused an east wind to blow across the land throughout that entire day and night; and when.

verses.kjv: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the coasts of Egypt: very grievous were they; before them there were no such locusts as they, neither after them shall be such.
verses.decoded: And the locusts spread over all the land of Egypt, and settled throughout all the regions of Egypt. They were extremely severe; there had never been such a swarm of locusts before them, nor will there ever be one like it again.

verses.kjv: For they covered the face of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened; and they did eat every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left: and there remained not any green thing in the trees, or in the herbs of the field, through all the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: For they covered the surface of the entire land, causing the land to become dark; and they consumed every plant in the land, and all the fruit from the trees that the hail had spared; and no green vegetation remained on the trees or among the plants in the fields throughout all the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste; and he said, I have sinned against the LORD your God, and against you.
verses.decoded: Then Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, 'I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.'

verses.kjv: Now therefore forgive, I pray thee, my sin only this once, and intreat the LORD your God, that he may take away from me this death only.
verses.decoded: Therefore, please forgive my sin just this one time, and plead with the LORD your God that he might remove this deadly plague from me.

verses.kjv: And he went out from Pharaoh, and intreated the LORD.
verses.decoded: And he departed from Pharaoh, and pleaded with the Lord.

verses.kjv: And the LORD turned a mighty strong west wind, which took away the locusts, and cast them into the Red sea; there remained not one locust in all the coasts of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And the Lord caused a very powerful west wind to blow, which carried away the locusts and swept them into the Red Sea; not a single locust remained anywhere in the territory of Egypt.

verses.kjv: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel go.
verses.decoded: But the Lord made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, so he would not allow the Israelites to leave.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Extend your hand toward the sky, so that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, a darkness so intense that it can be physically perceived.'

verses.kjv: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days:
verses.decoded: Then Moses extended his hand toward the sky, and a dense darkness covered the entire land of Egypt for three days.

verses.kjv: They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.
verses.decoded: No one could see anyone else, and for three days, no one got up from where they were. However, all the descendants of Israel had light in their homes.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh called unto Moses, and said, Go ye, serve the LORD; only let your flocks and your herds be stayed: let your little ones also go with you.
verses.decoded: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, 'Go and worship the LORD; however, your flocks and herds must remain behind. Let your children also go with you.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said, Thou must give us also sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice unto the LORD our God.
verses.decoded: And Moses said, You must also provide us with sacrifices and burnt offerings, so that we may offer sacrifices to the Lord our God.

verses.kjv: Our cattle also shall go with us; there shall not an hoof be left behind; for thereof must we take to serve the LORD our God; and we know not with what we must serve the LORD, until we come thither.
verses.decoded: Our livestock will also go with us; not a single animal will be left behind, because from them we must take what is needed to worship the LORD our God, and we do not know exactly what we will need to worship the LORD until we arrive there.

verses.kjv: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let them go.
verses.decoded: However, the Lord made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he would not allow them to depart.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh said unto him, Get thee from me, take heed to thyself, see my face no more; for in that day thou seest my face thou shalt die.
verses.decoded: And Pharaoh said to him, 'Leave my presence, be careful, and do not appear before me again; because on the day you see my face again, you will die.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said, Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more.
verses.decoded: And Moses said, 'You have spoken correctly; I will not see you again.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt; afterwards he will let you go hence: when he shall let you go, he shall surely thrust you out hence altogether.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, 'I will bring one more plague upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. After this, he will let you leave this place. When he lets you go, he will certainly drive you out of this place completely.'

verses.kjv: Speak now in the ears of the people, and let every man borrow of his neighbour, and every woman of her neighbour, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold.
verses.decoded: Now, tell the people that every man should request from his neighbor, and every woman from her neighbor, items made of silver and items made of gold.

verses.kjv: And the LORD gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants, and in the sight of the people.
verses.decoded: The Lord made the people well-regarded by the Egyptians. Furthermore, Moses was highly esteemed throughout the land of Egypt, both by Pharaoh's officials and by the general populace.

verses.kjv: And Moses said, Thus saith the LORD, About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt:
verses.decoded: And Moses said, 'This is what the LORD says: Around midnight I will go out into the middle of Egypt.'

verses.kjv: And all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the first born of Pharaoh that sitteth upon his throne, even unto the firstborn of the maidservant that is behind the mill; and all the firstborn of beasts.
verses.decoded: And every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn son of Pharaoh, who sits on his throne, all the way to the firstborn of the female servant who grinds at the mill; and all the firstborn of the livestock as well.

verses.kjv: And there shall be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there was none like it, nor shall be like it any more.
verses.decoded: And there will be a great outcry throughout the entire land of Egypt, such as there has never been, nor will there ever be again.

verses.kjv: But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the LORD doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.
verses.decoded: But as for the Israelites, not a dog will bark at them, whether at a person or an animal, so that you may know that the LORD makes a distinction between the Egyptians and the Israelites.

verses.kjv: And all these thy servants shall come down unto me, and bow down themselves unto me, saying, Get thee out, and all the people that follow thee: and after that I will go out. And he went out from Pharaoh in a great anger.
verses.decoded: Then all these officials of yours will come down to me and bow before me, saying, 'Leave, you and all the people who follow you.' And after that, I will depart.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you; that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord said to Moses, Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that my miraculous deeds may be increased in the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh: and the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, so that he would not let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.decoded: Moses and Aaron performed all these miraculous signs in Pharaoh's presence. Yet, the Lord made Pharaoh's heart unyielding, so that he refused to allow the Israelites to leave his country.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.decoded: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying:

verses.kjv: This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.
verses.decoded: This month will be for you the first of the months; it will be the first month of your year.

verses.kjv: Speak ye unto all the congregation of Israel, saying, In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to the house of their fathers, a lamb for an house:
verses.decoded: Tell the entire community of Israel that on the tenth day of this month, each man is to take a lamb for his family, one lamb per household.

verses.kjv: And if the household be too little for the lamb, let him and his neighbour next unto his house take it according to the number of the souls; every man according to his eating shall make your count for the lamb.
verses.decoded: If a household is too small to consume an entire lamb, then the head of that household and his closest neighbor should share one, dividing it according to the number of people in their households; each person's estimated consumption should determine their portion of the lamb.

verses.kjv: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year: ye shall take it out from the sheep, or from the goats:
verses.decoded: Your lamb must be without defect, a male in its first year of life; you must select it from either the sheep or the goats.

verses.kjv: And ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it in the evening.
verses.decoded: And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of that same month, and the entire assembly of the community of Israel shall slaughter it in the evening.

verses.kjv: And they shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.
verses.decoded: They are to take some of the blood and apply it to the two side posts and the upper door post of the houses where they will eat it.

verses.kjv: And they shall eat the flesh in that night, roast with fire, and unleavened bread; and with bitter herbs they shall eat it.
verses.decoded: And on that night, they are to eat the meat roasted over a fire, along with bread made without yeast, and they are to eat it with bitter herbs.

verses.kjv: Eat not of it raw, nor sodden at all with water, but roast with fire; his head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof.
verses.decoded: Do not eat it uncooked, nor boiled in water at all, but roast it over a fire, including its head, its legs, and its internal organs.

verses.kjv: And ye shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; and that which remaineth of it until the morning ye shall burn with fire.
verses.decoded: And you shall not let any of it remain until the morning; and whatever remains of it until the morning, you shall burn with fire.

verses.kjv: And thus shall ye eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD’s passover.
verses.decoded: And this is how you are to eat it: with your garments secured around your waist, your sandals on your feet, and your walking stick in your hand; and you must eat it quickly, because it is the Lord's Passover.

verses.kjv: For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the LORD.
verses.decoded: Because I will travel through the land of Egypt tonight, and I will strike down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal; and I will carry out judgment against all the gods of Egypt: I am the Lord.

verses.kjv: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: The blood will serve as a sign for you on the houses where you reside. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no destructive plague will come upon you when I strike the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to the LORD throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.
verses.decoded: This day will serve as a remembrance for you. You must observe it as a festival to the Lord for all your future generations; you must observe it as a festival by a lasting decree.

verses.kjv: Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.
verses.decoded: For seven days, you must eat bread made without yeast. On the first day, you must remove all yeast from your homes, because anyone who eats bread made with yeast from the first day until the seventh day will be expelled from the community of Israel.

verses.kjv: And in the first day there shall be an holy convocation, and in the seventh day there shall be an holy convocation to you; no manner of work shall be done in them, save that which every man must eat, that only may be done of you.
verses.decoded: On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly, and on the seventh day there is to be a sacred assembly for you. No kind of work is to be done on these days, except for what each person must eat; only that may be prepared by you.

verses.kjv: And ye shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this selfsame day have I brought your armies out of the land of Egypt: therefore shall ye observe this day in your generations by an ordinance for ever.
verses.decoded: You must observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. Therefore, you must observe this day throughout your generations as a permanent decree.

verses.kjv: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, ye shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the month at even.
verses.decoded: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of that month, in the evening, you must eat bread made without yeast, until the evening of the twenty-first day of the month.

verses.kjv: Seven days shall there be no leaven found in your houses: for whosoever eateth that which is leavened, even that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he be a stranger, or born in the land.
verses.decoded: For seven days, no leavening agent should be found in your homes. Because anyone who eats something that has been leavened, that person will be expelled from the community of Israel, whether they are a foreigner or a native-born Israelite.

verses.kjv: Ye shall eat nothing leavened; in all your habitations shall ye eat unleavened bread.
verses.decoded: You must not eat anything that contains leaven; in all your dwellings, you must eat bread made without leaven.

verses.kjv: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said unto them, Draw out and take you a lamb according to your families, and kill the passover.
verses.decoded: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and said to them, 'Select and take a lamb for yourselves for each of your households, and slaughter the Passover lamb.'

verses.kjv: And ye shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the bason, and strike the lintel and the two side posts with the blood that is in the bason; and none of you shall go out at the door of his house until the morning.
verses.decoded: You are to take a bundle of hyssop, dip it into the blood that is in the basin, and apply the blood from the basin to the top doorframe and the two doorposts; and no one among you is to leave the entrance of their house until morning.

verses.kjv: For the LORD will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the LORD will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.
verses.decoded: For the Lord will go through to strike down the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the top part of the doorframe, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the entrance.

verses.kjv: And ye shall observe this thing for an ordinance to thee and to thy sons for ever.
verses.decoded: And you must observe this practice as a permanent decree for you and your descendants for all time.

verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, when ye be come to the land which the LORD will give you, according as he hath promised, that ye shall keep this service.
verses.decoded: And it will come about that when you have entered the land which the Lord will give you, just as he has promised, you must observe this ritual.

verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, when your children shall say unto you, What mean ye by this service?
verses.decoded: And it will happen that when your children ask you, 'What do you mean by this ritual?'

verses.kjv: That ye shall say, It is the sacrifice of the LORD’s passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he smote the Egyptians, and delivered our houses. And the people bowed the head and worshipped.
verses.decoded: You are to say, 'This is the sacrifice for the Lord's Passover, because he passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when he struck down the Egyptians and spared our homes.' And the people bowed down and worshipped.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel went away, and did as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.
verses.decoded: And the people of Israel departed and carried out everything that the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron; they did exactly as instructed.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that at midnight the LORD smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.
verses.decoded: And it happened that at midnight, the LORD struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn son of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner who was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of animals.

verses.kjv: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.
verses.decoded: And Pharaoh got up during the night, along with all his officials and all the Egyptians; and there was a loud wailing throughout Egypt, because there was not a single household where no one had died.

verses.kjv: And he called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Rise up, and get you forth from among my people, both ye and the children of Israel; and go, serve the LORD, as ye have said.
verses.decoded: During the night, he summoned Moses and Aaron and told them, 'Get up and leave my people, both you and the Israelites. Go and worship the LORD, just as you requested.'

verses.kjv: Also take your flocks and your herds, as ye have said, and be gone; and bless me also.
verses.decoded: Also take your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and depart; and bless me as well.

verses.kjv: And the Egyptians were urgent upon the people, that they might send them out of the land in haste; for they said, We be all dead men.
verses.decoded: The Egyptians strongly urged the people to send them out of the country quickly, because they said, "We will all die."

verses.kjv: And the people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneadingtroughs being bound up in their clothes upon their shoulders.
verses.decoded: The people took their dough before it had risen, carrying their kneading bowls, wrapped in their garments, on their shoulders.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment:
verses.decoded: The Israelites did as Moses had instructed; they asked the Egyptians for articles made of silver, articles made of gold, and clothing.

verses.kjv: And the LORD gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.
verses.decoded: And the Lord caused the people to find favor with the Egyptians, so that the Egyptians lent them everything they requested. In doing so, the Israelites took valuable items from the Egyptians.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children.
verses.decoded: The Israelites traveled from Rameses to Succoth, approximately six hundred thousand adult males on foot, in addition to children.

verses.kjv: And a mixed multitude went up also with them; and flocks, and herds, even very much cattle.
verses.decoded: A diverse crowd of people also departed with them, along with a great many flocks and herds of livestock.

verses.kjv: And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought forth out of Egypt, for it was not leavened; because they were thrust out of Egypt, and could not tarry, neither had they prepared for themselves any victual.
verses.decoded: And they baked flatbreads made from the dough they had carried out of Egypt, because the dough had not risen; for they were expelled from Egypt and could not delay, nor had they prepared any food for themselves.

verses.kjv: Now the sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
verses.decoded: The period of time that the descendants of Israel resided in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of the LORD went out from the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And it happened that at the end of four hundred and thirty years, on that very same day, all the multitudes of the Lord departed from the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: It is a night to be much observed unto the LORD for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is that night of the LORD to be observed of all the children of Israel in their generations.
verses.decoded: This is a night to be greatly commemorated in honor of the Lord, because He brought them out of the land of Egypt. This is the Lord's night, which all the descendants of Israel are to commemorate throughout their generations.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses and Aaron, This is the ordinance of the passover: There shall no stranger eat thereof:
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, 'This is the regulation for the Passover: No foreigner shall eat of it.'

verses.kjv: But every man’s servant that is bought for money, when thou hast circumcised him, then shall he eat thereof.
verses.decoded: However, any male slave purchased with money, once you have circumcised him, may then eat of it.

verses.kjv: A foreigner and an hired servant shall not eat thereof.
verses.decoded: A temporary resident or a hired worker is not permitted to eat of it.

verses.kjv: In one house shall it be eaten; thou shalt not carry forth ought of the flesh abroad out of the house; neither shall ye break a bone thereof.
verses.decoded: It must be eaten within one house; you shall not carry any of the meat outside the house; nor shall you break any of its bones.

verses.kjv: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.
verses.decoded: The entire community of Israel must observe it.

verses.kjv: And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to the LORD, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: for no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.
verses.decoded: And if a foreigner resides among you and wishes to observe the Passover to the Lord, all his males must be circumcised. Then he may approach and observe it, and he will be considered as a native-born inhabitant of the land, because no uncircumcised person may eat of it.

verses.kjv: One law shall be to him that is homeborn, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among you.
verses.decoded: There shall be one law for the native-born and for the foreigner who lives among you.

verses.kjv: Thus did all the children of Israel; as the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron, so did they.
verses.decoded: All the Israelites did this, just as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they obeyed.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass the selfsame day, that the LORD did bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.
verses.decoded: And on that very same day, the Lord brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt in their organized groups.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.decoded: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.kjv: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.
verses.decoded: Set apart for me every firstborn, the first offspring to be born from a mother among the Israelites, both human and animal; it belongs to me.

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the LORD brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten.
verses.decoded: Then Moses said to the people, 'Remember this day, on which you came out of Egypt, out of the place of slavery, because by the power of his hand the Lord brought you out from this place. No bread made with yeast shall be eaten.'

verses.kjv: This day came ye out in the month Abib.
verses.decoded: On this day, you are departing in the month of Abib.

verses.kjv: And it shall be when the LORD shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.
verses.decoded: And it will happen that when the Lord brings you into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which he promised with an oath to your ancestors to give to you—a land abundant with milk and honey—then you must observe this ritual in this month.

verses.kjv: Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to the LORD.
verses.decoded: For seven days, you must eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day, there will be a special celebration dedicated to the Lord.

verses.kjv: Unleavened bread shall be eaten seven days; and there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.
verses.decoded: Bread made without yeast must be eaten for seven days; no bread made with yeast should be seen with you, nor should any yeast be seen with you throughout all your dwelling places.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the LORD did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And you shall explain to your son on that day, saying, 'This is done because of what the Lord did for me when I came out of Egypt.'

verses.kjv: And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the LORD’s law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath the LORD brought thee out of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And it will serve as a sign for you on your hand, and as a reminder between your eyes, so that the law of the LORD may be in your mouth, because with a powerful hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.

verses.kjv: Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year.
verses.decoded: Therefore, you must observe this regulation at its appointed time, year after year.

verses.kjv: And it shall be when the LORD shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, as he sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,
verses.decoded: And it will happen when the Lord brings you into the land of the Canaanites, as he promised you and your ancestors with an oath, and gives it to you.

verses.kjv: That thou shalt set apart unto the LORD all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the LORD’s.
verses.decoded: You are to dedicate to the Lord every firstborn that emerges from the womb, and every firstborn animal from your livestock; specifically, the male firstborns shall belong to the Lord.

verses.kjv: And every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break his neck: and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem.
verses.decoded: And every firstborn of a donkey you must redeem with a lamb; and if you do not redeem it, then you must break its neck; and all the firstborn of humans among your children you must redeem.

verses.kjv: And it shall be when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? that thou shalt say unto him, By strength of hand the LORD brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage:
verses.decoded: And when your son asks you in the future, saying, 'What is this?' you shall tell him, 'The LORD brought us out of Egypt, from the place of slavery, with a powerful hand.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, that the LORD slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of beast: therefore I sacrifice to the LORD all that openeth the matrix, being males; but all the firstborn of my children I redeem.
verses.decoded: And so it happened that when Pharaoh was very reluctant to let us leave, the Lord killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, including both the firstborn of people and the firstborn of animals.

verses.kjv: And it shall be for a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand the LORD brought us forth out of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And it will serve as a sign on your hand and as a reminder between your eyes, because the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:
verses.decoded: And so it happened, when Pharaoh had allowed the people to leave, that God did not lead them by way of the land of the Philistines, even though it was geographically close; for God said, 'So that the people do not change their minds if they encounter war, and then return to Egypt:'

verses.kjv: But God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: However, God guided the people by a circuitous route, through the wilderness area near the Red Sea. And the descendants of Israel departed from the land of Egypt in an organized and prepared manner.

verses.kjv: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.
verses.decoded: And Moses took Joseph's bones with him, because Joseph had made the Israelites solemnly promise, saying, "God will certainly come to your aid, and you must carry my bones away from this place."

verses.kjv: And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.
verses.decoded: They departed from Succoth and set up camp in Etham, at the edge of the wilderness.

verses.kjv: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:
verses.decoded: And the Lord led them during the day in a column of cloud to guide their journey, and during the night in a column of fire to provide them with light, so that they could travel both day and night.

verses.kjv: He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.
verses.decoded: He did not remove the column of cloud that guided them by day, nor the column of fire that guided them by night, from leading the people.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.decoded: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.kjv: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they turn and encamp before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, over against Baalzephon: before it shall ye encamp by the sea.
verses.decoded: Tell the Israelites to turn back and set up camp in front of Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, directly opposite Baal-zephon. You are to camp by the sea, facing it.

verses.kjv: For Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, They are entangled in the land, the wilderness hath shut them in.
verses.decoded: Because Pharaoh will say about the Israelites, 'They are confused in the land; the wilderness has trapped them.'

verses.kjv: And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, that he shall follow after them; and I will be honoured upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host; that the Egyptians may know that I am the LORD. And they did so.
verses.decoded: And I will make Pharaoh stubborn, so that he will pursue them; and I will gain glory through Pharaoh and all his army, so that the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD. And they did as I said.

verses.kjv: And it was told the king of Egypt that the people fled: and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was turned against the people, and they said, Why have we done this, that we have let Israel go from serving us?
verses.decoded: When the king of Egypt was informed that the people had escaped, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about the people. They said, "Why did we do this? Why did we let Israel leave our service?"

verses.kjv: And he made ready his chariot, and took his people with him:
verses.decoded: And he prepared his chariot, and brought his people along with him.

verses.kjv: And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over every one of them.
verses.decoded: And he took six hundred specially selected chariots, and all the other chariots in Egypt, along with officers in charge of each of them.

verses.kjv: And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel: and the children of Israel went out with an high hand.
verses.decoded: And the Lord made Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, resolute, and he pursued the people of Israel. However, the people of Israel departed with great confidence.

verses.kjv: But the Egyptians pursued after them, all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his army, and overtook them encamping by the sea, beside Pihahiroth, before Baalzephon.
verses.decoded: However, the Egyptians pursued them with all of Pharaoh's horses and chariots, his horsemen, and his army, and caught up with them as they were camped by the sea.

verses.kjv: And when Pharaoh drew nigh, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and, behold, the Egyptians marched after them; and they were sore afraid: and the children of Israel cried out unto the LORD.
verses.decoded: As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them; they were extremely frightened.

verses.kjv: And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt?
verses.decoded: And they said to Moses, "Is it because there were no burial places in Egypt that you have led us out here to die in the wilderness? Why have you treated us this way, bringing us out of Egypt?"

verses.kjv: Is not this the word that we did tell thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.
verses.decoded: Didn't we tell you this in Egypt, saying, 'Leave us alone so we can serve the Egyptians?' Because it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.
verses.decoded: And Moses said to the people, 'Do not be afraid. Stand firm and witness the Lord's deliverance, which he will show you today, because the Egyptians you see today, you will never see them again.'

verses.kjv: The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.
verses.decoded: The Lord will fight for you, and you are to remain silent.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Wherefore criest thou unto me? speak unto the children of Israel, that they go forward:
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, 'Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites to move forward.'

verses.kjv: But lift thou up thy rod, and stretch out thine hand over the sea, and divide it: and the children of Israel shall go on dry ground through the midst of the sea.
verses.decoded: But lift up your staff, and stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it; and the Israelites will walk on dry ground through the middle of the sea.

verses.kjv: And I, behold, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall follow them: and I will get me honour upon Pharaoh, and upon all his host, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.
verses.decoded: And indeed, I will make the Egyptians stubborn, and they will pursue the Israelites. And I will achieve glory for myself through Pharaoh and his entire army,

verses.kjv: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I have gotten me honour upon Pharaoh, upon his chariots, and upon his horsemen.
verses.decoded: And the Egyptians will come to understand that I am the Lord, when I have achieved recognition for myself through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his cavalry.

verses.kjv: And the angel of God, which went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them:
verses.decoded: Then the angel of God, who had been leading the Israelite camp, moved and went to their rear; and the pillar of cloud moved from in front of them and positioned itself behind them.

verses.kjv: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these: so that the one came not near the other all the night.
verses.decoded: And it positioned itself between the Egyptian army's encampment and the Israelite army's encampment; it appeared as a cloud and brought darkness to the Egyptians, but it provided light throughout the night for the Israelites, so that neither group could approach the other during the entire night.

verses.kjv: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
verses.decoded: Then Moses extended his hand over the sea; and God made the sea retreat by means of a powerful east wind throughout that entire night, turning the sea into dry ground, and the waters were separated.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
verses.decoded: The Israelites walked into the middle of the sea on dry ground, with the water forming a wall on their right and on their left.

verses.kjv: And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, even all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.
verses.decoded: The Egyptians chased them and entered the middle of the sea after them, specifically all of Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his cavalry.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that in the morning watch the LORD looked unto the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubled the host of the Egyptians,
verses.decoded: Then, during the morning watch, the Lord observed the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and cloud, and caused confusion among the Egyptian army.

verses.kjv: And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the LORD fighteth for them against the Egyptians.
verses.decoded: And He caused their chariot wheels to come off, so that they had great difficulty driving them. As a result, the Egyptians said, 'Let us run away from the Israelites, because the LORD is fighting for them against us Egyptians.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, 'Extend your hand over the sea, so that the waters may return over the Egyptians, over their chariots and their horsemen.'

verses.kjv: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and the LORD overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.
verses.decoded: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its full force as morning dawned; and the Egyptians fled into it; and the Lord overwhelmed the Egyptians in the middle of the sea.

verses.kjv: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.
verses.decoded: The waters flowed back and covered the chariots, the horsemen, and all of Pharaoh's army that had pursued them into the sea; not a single one of them survived.

verses.kjv: But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea; and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
verses.decoded: However, the descendants of Israel walked on dry ground through the middle of the sea; and the water formed a protective barrier for them on both their right side and their left side.

verses.kjv: Thus the LORD saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.
verses.decoded: In this way, the Lord rescued the Israelites that day from the power of the Egyptians; and the Israelites saw the Egyptians lying dead on the seashore.

verses.kjv: And Israel saw that great work which the LORD did upon the Egyptians: and the people feared the LORD, and believed the LORD, and his servant Moses.
verses.decoded: And the people of Israel witnessed the powerful act that the Lord performed against the Egyptians; and the people held the Lord in awe, and they put their trust in the Lord and in his servant Moses.

verses.kjv: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD, and spake, saying, I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
verses.decoded: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the Lord, and they declared, 'I will sing to the Lord, for he has achieved a magnificent victory; he has cast the horse and its rider into the sea.'

verses.kjv: The LORD is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God, and I will prepare him an habitation; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.
verses.decoded: The Lord is my source of strength and my song of praise; he has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will make a dwelling place for him; he is the God of my father, and I will honor him greatly.

verses.kjv: The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name.
verses.decoded: The Lord is a warrior; the Lord is his name.

verses.kjv: Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.
verses.decoded: He has thrown Pharaoh's chariots and his army into the sea; also, his finest officers have drowned in the Red Sea.

verses.kjv: The depths have covered them: they sank into the bottom as a stone.
verses.decoded: The deep waters submerged them; they sank to the bottom like a stone.

verses.kjv: Thy right hand, O LORD, is become glorious in power: thy right hand, O LORD, hath dashed in pieces the enemy.
verses.decoded: Your right hand, O Lord, has become magnificent in strength; your right hand, O Lord, has shattered the enemy.

verses.kjv: And in the greatness of thine excellency thou hast overthrown them that rose up against thee: thou sentest forth thy wrath, which consumed them as stubble.
verses.decoded: And with your immense majesty, you have defeated those who rose up against you; you unleashed your fierce anger, which consumed them like dry stubble.

verses.kjv: And with the blast of thy nostrils the waters were gathered together, the floods stood upright as an heap, and the depths were congealed in the heart of the sea.
verses.decoded: And at the powerful blast from your nostrils, the waters gathered together; the flowing waters stood upright like a mound, and the deep parts of the sea became solid in its midst.

verses.kjv: The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; my lust shall be satisfied upon them; I will draw my sword, my hand shall destroy them.
verses.decoded: The enemy declared, 'I will chase, I will catch up, I will divide the plunder; my desire will be satisfied by them; I will draw my sword, my hand will destroy them.'

verses.kjv: Thou didst blow with thy wind, the sea covered them: they sank as lead in the mighty waters.
verses.decoded: You blew with your wind, the sea covered them; they sank like lead in the powerful waters.

verses.kjv: Who is like unto thee, O LORD, among the gods? who is like thee, glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders?
verses.decoded: Who is like you, O Lord, among the divine beings? Who is like you, magnificent in holiness, awe-inspiring in the praises offered to you, performing wonders?

verses.kjv: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them.
verses.decoded: You stretched out your right hand, and the earth swallowed them.

verses.kjv: Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people which thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided them in thy strength unto thy holy habitation.
verses.decoded: You, in your compassion, have led out the people whom you have rescued; you have guided them with your power to your sacred dwelling place.

verses.kjv: The people shall hear, and be afraid: sorrow shall take hold on the inhabitants of Palestina.
verses.decoded: The people will hear and be afraid; distress will seize the inhabitants of Philistia.

verses.kjv: Then the dukes of Edom shall be amazed; the mighty men of Moab, trembling shall take hold upon them; all the inhabitants of Canaan shall melt away.
verses.decoded: Then the chiefs of Edom will be terrified; the powerful men of Moab will be seized with trembling; all the people living in Canaan will lose their courage.

verses.kjv: Fear and dread shall fall upon them; by the greatness of thine arm they shall be as still as a stone; till thy people pass over, O LORD, till the people pass over, which thou hast purchased.
verses.decoded: Fear and terror will overcome them; by your mighty power, they will become as still as a stone, until your people cross over, O Lord, until the people whom you have acquired cross over.

verses.kjv: Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thine inheritance, in the place, O LORD, which thou hast made for thee to dwell in, in the Sanctuary, O LORD, which thy hands have established.
verses.decoded: You will bring them in and establish them on the mountain of your inheritance, in the place, O Lord, which you have made for yourself to live in, in the sanctuary, O Lord, which your hands have prepared.

verses.kjv: The LORD shall reign for ever and ever.
verses.decoded: The Lord will reign forever.

verses.kjv: For the horse of Pharaoh went in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and the LORD brought again the waters of the sea upon them; but the children of Israel went on dry land in the midst of the sea.
verses.decoded: Because Pharaoh's horses, along with his chariots and his horsemen, entered the sea, the Lord caused the waters of the sea to return and cover them; however, the people of Israel walked on dry ground through the middle of the sea.

verses.kjv: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.
verses.decoded: And Miriam, who was a prophetess and Aaron's sister, took a tambourine in her hand; and all the other women followed her, playing tambourines and dancing.

verses.kjv: And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
verses.decoded: And Miriam responded to them, 'Sing to the Lord, for he has achieved a magnificent victory; he has thrown the horse and its rider into the sea.'

verses.kjv: So Moses brought Israel from the Red sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
verses.decoded: So Moses led the Israelites away from the Red Sea, and they traveled into the Desert of Shur. They journeyed for three days in the desert and did not find any water.

verses.kjv: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah.
verses.decoded: And when they arrived at Marah, they could not drink the water from there because it was bitter; consequently, the place was named Marah.

verses.kjv: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?
verses.decoded: And the people complained to Moses, asking, 'What are we going to drink?'

verses.kjv: And he cried unto the LORD; and the LORD shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet: there he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them,
verses.decoded: And he called out to the Lord; and the Lord showed him a tree, which, when he threw it into the water, the water became drinkable. There he established for them a law and a regulation, and there he tested them.

verses.kjv: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that healeth thee.
verses.decoded: And He said, "If you will carefully listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and pay attention to His commands, and obey all His decrees, I will not inflict upon you any of the diseases that I brought upon the Egyptians, for I am the LORD who heals you."

verses.kjv: And they came to Elim, where were twelve wells of water, and threescore and ten palm trees: and they encamped there by the waters.
verses.decoded: And they arrived at Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and they set up camp there by the water sources.

verses.kjv: And they took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came unto the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And they departed from Elim, and the entire community of the Israelites arrived at the Wilderness of Sin, which is located between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departure from the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv: And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness:
verses.decoded: And the entire community of the Israelites complained against Moses and Aaron in the desert.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel said unto them, Would to God we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the flesh pots, and when we did eat bread to the full; for ye have brought us forth into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.
verses.decoded: And the Israelites said to them, "We wish we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat beside the pots of meat and ate as much bread as we wanted; for you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this entire community with hunger."

verses.kjv: Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.
verses.decoded: Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Look, I will cause bread to fall from the sky for you; and the people must go out and collect a specific amount each day, so that I can test them, to see if they will follow my instructions or not.'

verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, that on the sixth day they shall prepare that which they bring in; and it shall be twice as much as they gather daily.
verses.decoded: It will happen that on the sixth day, they will prepare what they have collected, and it will be twice the amount they gather daily.

verses.kjv: And Moses and Aaron said unto all the children of Israel, At even, then ye shall know that the LORD hath brought you out from the land of Egypt:
verses.decoded: Moses and Aaron told all the people of Israel, 'This evening, you will know that the LORD has led you out of Egypt.'

verses.kjv: And in the morning, then ye shall see the glory of the LORD; for that he heareth your murmurings against the LORD: and what are we, that ye murmur against us?
verses.decoded: And in the morning, you will then see the magnificent presence of the Lord; because he hears your complaints against the Lord: and what are we, that you complain against us?

verses.kjv: And Moses said, This shall be, when the LORD shall give you in the evening flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full; for that the LORD heareth your murmurings which ye murmur against him: and what are we? your murmurings are not against us, but against the LORD.
verses.decoded: Then Moses said, "This will happen when the Lord provides you with meat to eat in the evening and plenty of bread in the morning, because the Lord has heard your complaints that you are making against him. What are we? Your complaints are not against us, but against the Lord."

verses.kjv: And Moses spake unto Aaron, Say unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, Come near before the LORD: for he hath heard your murmurings.
verses.decoded: And Moses spoke to Aaron, saying, 'Tell the entire assembly of the Israelites to come forward into the presence of the Lord, because he has heard your complaints.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, as Aaron spake unto the whole congregation of the children of Israel, that they looked toward the wilderness, and, behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud.
verses.decoded: And it happened that as Aaron spoke to the entire assembly of the people of Israel, they looked toward the desert, and suddenly, the magnificent presence of the Lord became visible in the cloud.

verses.kjv: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.decoded: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.kjv: I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel: speak unto them, saying, At even ye shall eat flesh, and in the morning ye shall be filled with bread; and ye shall know that I am the LORD your God.
verses.decoded: I have heard the complaints of the Israelites. Tell them that in the evening they will eat meat, and in the morning they will be filled with bread; then they will know that I am the LORD their God.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that at even the quails came up, and covered the camp: and in the morning the dew lay round about the host.
verses.decoded: And it happened that in the evening, quails appeared and covered the camp. And in the morning, dew lay all around the assembly.

verses.kjv: And when the dew that lay was gone up, behold, upon the face of the wilderness there lay a small round thing, as small as the hoar frost on the ground.
verses.decoded: And when the dew that had settled evaporated, then across the wilderness there was a small, round object, as tiny as the frost on the ground.

verses.kjv: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.
verses.decoded: And when the Israelites saw it, they said to each other, 'It is manna,' because they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, 'This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.'

verses.kjv: This is the thing which the LORD hath commanded, Gather of it every man according to his eating, an omer for every man, according to the number of your persons; take ye every man for them which are in his tents.
verses.decoded: This is what the Lord has commanded: Each person is to gather as much as they can eat, an omer for each person, according to the number of people you have. Each of you should take for those who are in your tents.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel did so, and gathered, some more, some less.
verses.decoded: And the Israelites did as instructed; some collected a larger amount, while others collected a smaller amount.

verses.kjv: And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.
verses.decoded: And when they measured it with an omer, the one who gathered a lot did not have too much, and the one who gathered a little did not have too little; each person gathered according to what they could eat.

verses.kjv: And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning.
verses.decoded: And Moses said, 'No one should leave any of it until the morning.'

verses.kjv: Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.
verses.decoded: However, they did not listen to Moses; instead, some of them left part of it until the morning, and it became full of worms and smelled foul. Consequently, Moses was angry with them.

verses.kjv: And they gathered it every morning, every man according to his eating: and when the sun waxed hot, it melted.
verses.decoded: And they collected it each morning, each person gathering enough for their own consumption; and when the sun became hot, it melted.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for one man: and all the rulers of the congregation came and told Moses.
verses.decoded: It happened that on the sixth day, they collected twice the usual amount of bread, specifically two omers for each person; and all the leaders of the community approached Moses and informed him of this.

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, This is that which the LORD hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
verses.decoded: And he said to them, 'This is what the LORD has commanded: Tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. Bake what you want to bake today, and boil what you want to boil; and whatever is left over, set aside for yourselves to be kept until the morning.'

verses.kjv: And they laid it up till the morning, as Moses bade: and it did not stink, neither was there any worm therein.
verses.decoded: And they stored it until the morning, just as Moses had commanded; and it did not spoil, nor were there any maggots in it.

verses.kjv: And Moses said, Eat that to day; for to day is a sabbath unto the LORD: to day ye shall not find it in the field.
verses.decoded: And Moses said, "Eat that today, because today is a Sabbath dedicated to the Lord; today you will not find it in the field."

verses.kjv: Six days ye shall gather it; but on the seventh day, which is the sabbath, in it there shall be none.
verses.decoded: For six days you are to gather it; however, on the seventh day, which is the Sabbath, there will be none of it to collect.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that there went out some of the people on the seventh day for to gather, and they found none.
verses.decoded: However, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather, but they found nothing.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, How long refuse ye to keep my commandments and my laws?
verses.decoded: Then the Lord said to Moses, "How much longer will you refuse to obey my commands and my instructions?"

verses.kjv: See, for that the LORD hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
verses.decoded: Understand that the Lord has given you the Sabbath; therefore, on the sixth day, he provides you with enough bread for two days. Everyone should remain in their dwelling; no one should leave their dwelling on the seventh day.

verses.kjv: So the people rested on the seventh day.
verses.decoded: Therefore, the people rested on the seventh day.

verses.kjv: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.
verses.decoded: The people of Israel named it Manna. It looked like white coriander seeds, and its taste was like flat cakes made with honey.

verses.kjv: And Moses said, This is the thing which the LORD commandeth, Fill an omer of it to be kept for your generations; that they may see the bread wherewith I have fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you forth from the land of Egypt.
verses.decoded: And Moses said, 'This is what the LORD commands: Fill an omer (a specific measure) of it to be preserved for your future generations, so that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I led you out of the land of Egypt.'

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omer full of manna therein, and lay it up before the LORD, to be kept for your generations.
verses.decoded: Then Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put one omer of manna into it, and place it before the Lord, so that it may be preserved for your future generations."

verses.kjv: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony, to be kept.
verses.decoded: Just as the Lord instructed Moses, Aaron placed it in front of the covenant tablets for safekeeping.

verses.kjv: And the children of Israel did eat manna forty years, until they came to a land inhabited; they did eat manna, until they came unto the borders of the land of Canaan.
verses.decoded: And the Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they arrived at an inhabited land; they continued to eat manna until they reached the borders of the land of Canaan.

verses.kjv: Now an omer is the tenth part of an ephah.
verses.decoded: An omer is equivalent to one-tenth of an ephah.

verses.kjv: And all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, after their journeys, according to the commandment of the LORD, and pitched in Rephidim: and there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.decoded: And the entire community of the Israelites traveled from the Wilderness of Sin, continuing their stages of travel as commanded by the LORD, and they set up camp in Rephidim; but there was no water there for the people to drink.

verses.kjv: Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said unto them, Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the LORD?
verses.decoded: Therefore, the people argued with Moses, saying, 'Give us water so we can drink.' And Moses said to them, 'Why are you arguing with me? Why are you testing the Lord?'

verses.kjv: And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?
verses.decoded: And the people there were thirsty for water; and the people complained against Moses, and said, 'Why have you brought us out of Egypt, only to kill us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?'

verses.kjv: And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me.
verses.decoded: Then Moses called out to the Lord, saying, 'What am I to do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me.'

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go on before the people, and take with thee of the elders of Israel; and thy rod, wherewith thou smotest the river, take in thine hand, and go.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, Go ahead of the people, and take some of the elders of Israel with you, and your staff, with which you struck the river,

verses.kjv: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it, that the people may drink. And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
verses.decoded: Indeed, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb; and you must strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people can drink.

verses.kjv: And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the LORD, saying, Is the LORD among us, or not?
verses.decoded: He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled and tested the Lord, saying,

verses.kjv: Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
verses.decoded: Afterward, Amalek arrived and engaged in battle with Israel at Rephidim.

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto Joshua, Choose us out men, and go out, fight with Amalek: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in mine hand.
verses.decoded: Then Moses said to Joshua, "Select some men for us, and go out and fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."

verses.kjv: So Joshua did as Moses had said to him, and fought with Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
verses.decoded: So, Joshua did exactly as Moses had instructed him and fought against the Amalekites. Meanwhile, Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
verses.decoded: And it happened that when Moses raised his hand, Israel was winning; but when he lowered his hand, Amalek was winning.

verses.kjv: But Moses’ hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.
verses.decoded: But Moses' arms became tired; so they brought a stone and placed it beneath him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on each side; and his hands remained steady until sunset.

verses.kjv: And Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
verses.decoded: And Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the sword.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
verses.decoded: And the Lord said to Moses, Write this as a record in a book, and repeat it to Joshua, because I will completely erase the memory of Amalek from the earth.

verses.kjv: And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it Jehovahnissi:
verses.decoded: And Moses constructed an altar, and he named it 'The Lord is my Banner'.

verses.kjv: For he said, Because the LORD hath sworn that the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
verses.decoded: For he said, because the Lord has sworn that the Lord will wage war against Amalek for all generations.

verses.kjv: When Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father in law, heard of all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people, and that the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt;
verses.decoded: When Jethro, who was a priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard about everything God had done for Moses and for his people, Israel, and how the Lord had led Israel out of Egypt.

verses.kjv: Then Jethro, Moses’ father in law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after he had sent her back,
verses.decoded: Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought Zipporah, Moses' wife, after Moses had sent her away.

verses.kjv: And her two sons; of which the name of the one was Gershom; for he said, I have been an alien in a strange land:
verses.decoded: And she had two sons; the name of one was Gershom, because Moses had said, 'I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.'

verses.kjv: And the name of the other was Eliezer; for the God of my father, said he, was mine help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh:
verses.decoded: And the other son was named Eliezer, because, he said, 'My father's God was my helper, and he rescued me from Pharaoh's sword.'

verses.kjv: And Jethro, Moses’ father in law, came with his sons and his wife unto Moses into the wilderness, where he encamped at the mount of God:
verses.decoded: And Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife to Moses in the wilderness, where Moses was camped at the mountain of God.

verses.kjv: And he said unto Moses, I thy father in law Jethro am come unto thee, and thy wife, and her two sons with her.
verses.decoded: And he said to Moses, 'I, your father-in-law Jethro, have come to you, along with your wife and her two sons.'

verses.kjv: And Moses went out to meet his father in law, and did obeisance, and kissed him; and they asked each other of their welfare; and they came into the tent.
verses.decoded: And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and he bowed down respectfully and kissed him. They each inquired about the other's well-being, and then they went into the tent.

verses.kjv: And Moses told his father in law all that the LORD had done unto Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, and all the travail that had come upon them by the way, and how the LORD delivered them.
verses.decoded: And Moses recounted to his father-in-law everything the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for the sake of Israel, and all the hardships that had come upon them during their journey.

verses.kjv: And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness which the LORD had done to Israel, whom he had delivered out of the hand of the Egyptians.
verses.decoded: Jethro celebrated all the good things the Lord had done for Israel, whom He had rescued from the power of the Egyptians.

verses.kjv: And Jethro said, Blessed be the LORD, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh, who hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.
verses.decoded: And Jethro said, 'Praise the Lord, who has rescued you from the control of the Egyptians, and from the control of Pharaoh, and who has rescued the people from the oppression of the Egyptians.'

verses.kjv: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them.
verses.decoded: Now I understand that the Lord is superior to all other deities, because in the very matter where they acted arrogantly, He proved Himself to be above them.

verses.kjv: And Jethro, Moses’ father in law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with Moses’ father in law before God.
verses.decoded: Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and other sacrifices to God. Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to share a meal with Moses' father-in-law.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses sat to judge the people: and the people stood by Moses from the morning unto the evening.
verses.decoded: The next day, Moses sat down to judge the people, and the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.

verses.kjv: And when Moses’ father in law saw all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? why sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand by thee from morning unto even?
verses.decoded: When Moses' father-in-law observed everything he was doing for the people, he asked, 'What is this activity you are performing for the people? Why are you sitting by yourself, while all the people stand around you all day long?'

verses.kjv: And Moses said unto his father in law, Because the people come unto me to enquire of God:
verses.decoded: And Moses said to his father-in-law, 'Because the people come to me to seek guidance from God.'

verses.kjv: When they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge between one and another, and I do make them know the statutes of God, and his laws.
verses.decoded: When people have a legal case or a dispute, they come to me, and I decide the case between individuals, and I inform them of God's decrees and his instructions.

verses.kjv: And Moses’ father in law said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good.
verses.decoded: Moses' father-in-law said to him, 'What you are doing is not good.'

verses.kjv: Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.
verses.decoded: You and the people with you will certainly become exhausted, because this task is too burdensome for you; you are not able to do it by yourself.

verses.kjv: Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God:
verses.decoded: Listen now to my advice, and God will be with you. You should represent the people before God, so that you can present their cases to God.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.
verses.decoded: And you shall instruct them in decrees and regulations, and you shall show them the path they must follow and the tasks they must perform.

verses.kjv: Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens:
verses.decoded: Furthermore, you must select from all the people capable men who respect God, trustworthy men who detest dishonest gain; and appoint such individuals over them to serve as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

verses.kjv: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee.
verses.decoded: And let them judge the people at all times. It will happen that they will bring every major issue to you, but they themselves will judge every minor issue. In this way, it will be easier for you, and they will share the burden with you.

verses.kjv: If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace.
verses.decoded: If you do this, and God so commands you, then you will be able to endure, and all these people will also go to their homes in peace.

verses.kjv: So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father in law, and did all that he had said.
verses.decoded: So Moses listened to the advice of his father-in-law and did everything he had told him to do.
